title: 1. Isolate exact-success ARS from dense-reward ARS
hypothesis: Exact-success ARS improves sustained success more than dense-reward ARS because it allocates parameter updates to crossing the episode-success boundary rather than increasing reward within unsuccessful episodes.

prediction.against: Contemporaneous dense-reward ARS with identical initialization, layout, directions and budget
prediction.rationale:
Ranked first for information per episode: this isolates the objective with substantially less simulation and no controller-generation calls; it is optional, not a prerequisite for P2. Unlike deferred R-105, this compares the exact success predicate against the original dense objective, uses 512 shared placements per signed candidate, and freezes terminal means without checkpoint selection. Run one matched search block: both arms start at zero residual on the frozen D-072 reference and receive 12 ARS updates, four antithetic directions, nu=0.02, alpha=0.01, identical normalization and common direction seeds. Change only the objective, retaining the original dense objective's documented components. Freeze both terminal means before evaluating either. Confirm both arms, the frozen R-106 finalist and D-072 on twelve fresh 128-case manifests: 1,536 paired cases. This provides at least approximately 80% unadjusted case-level power for a five-point effect under discordance up to 0.41, but one search block cannot establish population-level optimizer superiority. Keep training and confirmation disjoint and use the established one-whole-manifest-per-fresh-process evaluator. Preserve Stage 3, the sustained-success predicate, strict paired promotion and the one-sided 95% drop upper-bound requirement of <=0.05; never modify the saved incumbent. Report case-paired and manifest-level intervals, controls, failure categories, wins/losses/ties, residual execution, saturation, curves, resource use and reconstructable artifacts in research_result.json. Episode cost counts simulator starts, including resets: approximately 196,800 training starts, 12,288 confirmation starts and 4,096 smoke starts; ceiling 250,000. Seed arrays are deliberately unassigned at proposal time: atomically reserve 14 distinct seeds from the live ledger's free head, currently starting at 4820, before execution; populate and freeze the listed manifest templates. Run only after its new study handler and necessary tests exist, and never concurrently with P2. Existing escalation and exhaustion rules apply.

FROZEN REVISION (triage round 2, agreed; supersedes the text above where they differ). Seeds: 4820 smoke; 4821 the training placements (cases.placements(4821, 6144), 512 per update) AND the direction RNG (default_rng(4821 + 2000)), shared by both arms, so the two arms see identical placements and identical directions at update 1 and differ only through their own parameter trajectories; 4822-4833 twelve 128-case confirmation manifests config/manifests/pen_spin_stage3_objective_confirm_s<seed>.yaml. Arms, each its own persistent training process with R-106's child, layout (two 2,048-environment rollouts per update, 4 slots x the same 512 placements, first episode per environment), 12 updates, 4 antithetic directions all used, nu 0.02, alpha 0.01, zero initial residual on the D-072 reference, R-103 normalisation, bounds 0.10: (exact) return = sustained-success fraction of the candidate's 512 first episodes, as R-106; (dense) return = mean over its 512 first episodes of the summed R-103 step reward, sum_t [exp(-(d_t/0.08)^2) min(|w_t|/6, 1) - 0.01 mean_j((executed_j - reference_j)/0.10)^2], minus 5 on a fall. Each arm's terminal mean is frozen and hashed (finalists.json) before either is evaluated; no checkpoint selection. Smoke (seed 4820): R-106's gates plus a check that the dense return of the zero-theta slots is finite and that its A/A slot values agree to the reported tolerance. Confirmation: the reference, both terminal means and the frozen R-106 finalist, each once per manifest in a fresh process (48 cells, 1,536 pairs per contrast). Contrasts: exact minus dense (primary, the registered prediction); exact minus reference and dense minus reference (qualification; strict paired rule and one-sided 95% drop bound <= 0.05); Holm over those three; R-106 finalist minus reference reported as a descriptive replication bridge to D-075. Case-paired and manifest-clustered intervals for each. Budget: about 217,300 starts (training 2 x 98,400; smoke 8,200; confirmation 4 x 1,536 cases charged at 2 = 12,288); hard ceiling 250,000 enforced before every rollout; a started child is never relaunched from its seed. One matched search block: the conclusion is conditional on this pair of trajectories.

falsified_by: The predicted five-point advantage is refuted if the paired interval's upper bound is below +0.05; an interval spanning zero and +0.05 is inconclusive, not evidence that the objectives are equivalent. A lower bound above zero establishes a positive conditional effect, not necessarily an effect exceeding +0.05.

result.notes: Both arms saw identical placements and identical direction streams and differ only in the return ARS optimised; both terminal means were frozen in finalists.json before any confirmation case. Deviation: during confirmation one evaluation process (the reference on manifest s4825, the tenth cell) died at simulator start-up with 'malloc(): unaligned tcache chunk detected' before producing any result; the driver was rerun, skipped the 9 finished cells and ran the remaining 39; no training child was relaunched and nothing was re-scored (log kept as driver_crash_s4825.log). The dense arm optimises R-103's summed step reward and still raises the success count as much as the exact arm does: in training the two arms' candidate success curves are indistinguishable (0.39 -> 0.51) and each arm's finalist also scores well on the other arm's return; the two finalists point the same way (cosine 0.84). So D-075's gain is not explained by the exact-success objective; what R-106 and both arms here share, and R-103 lacked, is the instrument: 512 shared placements per signed candidate in one batch (A/A slot differences at most 0.016 here) and 17.6 M transitions per run, 38x R-103's. This also revises D-074's side remark: with a quiet enough contrast, the dense reward's policy-level misalignment does not stop ARS from finding success gains. The frozen R-106 finalist replicates on entirely new cases: +0.110 [+0.080, +0.140] (828 vs 659), descriptive, outside the Holm family. One matched pair of trajectories; charged starts 217,323 of 250,000; zero LLM calls.

verdicts.reasoning: Exact-success ARS minus dense-reward ARS, identical in placements, directions, layout and budget: -0.021 paired sustained success, 95% interval [-0.046, +0.005] over 1,536 fresh pairs (793 vs 825; 181 wins, 213 losses), manifest-clustered [-0.055, +0.014]. The upper bound is below the predicted +0.05 (and barely above zero), so the predicted advantage of the exact objective is refuted. Both arms beat the reference and pass both adoption gates: exact +0.087 [+0.058, +0.116], dense +0.108 [+0.080, +0.136], each positive in 12 of 12 manifests, Holm p < 1e-7, drops 46 and 51 against 74. The frozen R-106 finalist replicates on these new cases at +0.110 [+0.080, +0.140]. Conclusion: D-075's gain comes from the instrument (512 shared placements per signed candidate in one batch, 17.6 M transitions) rather than from the objective. One matched pair of trajectories.
verdicts.next_experiment: Run R-109 (P2) as approved; its inner learner (exact-success ARS in this layout) is a sound choice either way, and this result says the dense return would serve equally. For later ideas: P1's original comparison (PPO vs ARS vs draws) was confounded by the same instrument problem and could be rerun fairly now, but P2 comes first under the direction.

verdicts.reasoning: The named matched dense-reward control was measured: exact-minus-dense paired_success_difference was -0.02083 over 1,536 pairs, with a 95% case-paired interval of [-0.04617, +0.00450] [logs/pen_spin/r108_objective_attribution/summary.json]. The manifest-clustered interval was [-0.05531, +0.01364]; both upper bounds are below the registered +0.05 threshold, satisfying the stated falsification criterion [logs/pen_spin/r108_objective_attribution/summary.json]. Both intervals include zero, so the result establishes neither dense-objective superiority nor objective equivalence [logs/pen_spin/r108_objective_attribution/summary.json]. Exact and dense each qualified against the reference, improving paired success by +0.08724 and +0.10807 respectively while passing Holm correction and the drop gate, but those gains do not support an exact-objective advantage [logs/pen_spin/r108_objective_attribution/summary.json]. This is a trajectory-conditional result; it does not isolate batch size or training budget as the explanation for earlier gains [logs/pen_spin/r108_objective_attribution/frozen_config.json, logs/pen_spin/r108_objective_attribution/summary.json].

Use the frozen D-072-qualified controller as the experimental reference, without changing the saved default incumbent. First compare independent parameter draws, ARS/CEM and PPO on one identical sparse, state-conditioned symbolic residual family. If an inner learner produces a confirmed useful gain, compare fixed structure, grammar-based structural evolution and LLM-guided structural evolution with that learner and inherited parameters. Investigate compact memory or anchored component replacement only when the preceding results motivate them. Preserve the task, frozen evaluation manifests and strict paired promotion/drop criteria. Run one protocol at a time. No controller-generation LLM calls during P1; advisor calls for the research loop remain allowed. Later controller-generation calls need an agreed protocol and explicit call budget. Do not repeat R-102, retune its confirmation cases, reopen cold whole-controller generation, or resume expert cloning. Continue evidence-driven follow-ups within this direction through the existing loop, including its escalation and exhaustion rules.
